newsitem.title: USA: First Midwest to buy SparBank for $105 mln.
newsitem.headline: First Midwest to buy SparBank for $105 mln.

text.p: First Midwest Bancorp Inc said Friday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire SparBank Inc, the holding company of the $445 million McHenry State Bank in McHenry, Ill.

As part of the $105 million deal, SparBank shareholders will each receive 21.72 shares of First Midwest common stock, resulting in the issuance of 3,230,769 First Midwest shares. The acquisition will be structured as a tax-free exchange and accounted for as a pooling of interests.
The deal is expected to close by September 30, following receipt of customary regulatory approvals.

First Midwest said the transaction is expected to be neutral to its 1997 earnings and two to three percent accretive to 1998 results. The accretion is based on projected annualized net cost savings of about $1.8 million, representing some 18 percent of McHenry State Bank's current expense base.

First Midwest said it expects to take a pretax merger-related charge of about $6.5 million in the quarter in which the transaction closes. The charge will include systems conversions, elimination of excess operating capacity, professional fees and a one-time provision to bring McHenry State Bank's loan loss reserves to First Midwest's required levels.
The agreement has been approved by both the board and shareholders of SparBank and the board of First Midwest. First Midwest shareholder approval is not necessary.
In connection with the agreement, First Midwest's board rescinded the balance of the 900,000 share stock repurchase program authorized in November 1996.
With the acquisition, First Midwest's assets increase to approximately $3.5 billion.
